title: Direct Identifiability via GPS Location Data
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from the child's device can directly identify the child's precise location, movements, and patterns of behavior, enabling identification of the child as a specific individual.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted with sufficient precision to identify specific locations

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Live GPS coordinates may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend system breaches, inadequate access controls, or improper data sharing practices.
assumptions: Backend system has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Linkability of Location Data Points
description: Multiple GPS data points transmitted at regular intervals can be linked together to reconstruct detailed movement patterns, daily routines, and behavioral profiles of the child.
assumptions: Data points are transmitted with timestamps and sufficient frequency for pattern analysis

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Children's Data
description: Processing live GPS data of a child may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws requiring special protections for minors' location information.
assumptions: Applicable child privacy regulations require explicit consent and additional safeguards for location data

title: Inadequate Data Protection in Backend Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend may lack sufficient encryption, access controls, or data retention policies to protect the sensitive GPS location data during storage and processing.
assumptions: Backend implementation may have security gaps or insufficient privacy-by-design measures

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location History
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or insider threats.
assumptions: Access controls on DS1 are not properly implemented or are bypassed

title: Location Data Tampering
description: Stored location history in DS1 could be modified or deleted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially enabling location spoofing attacks.
assumptions: DS1 lacks adequate integrity controls and audit logging

title: Direct Identification from Location Data
description: Location history data in DS1 could directly identify individuals through unique location patterns, timestamps, or geolocation precision.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Location Data
description: Location history in DS1 could be linked with other data sources (e.g., device IDs, user accounts) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals' movements and behaviors.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other identifiers

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Store
description: Unauthorized actors could gain access to DS1 to view, copy, or exfiltrate location history data without proper authentication and authorization.
assumptions: DS1 authentication mechanisms are weak or bypassed

title: Inappropriate Data Retention
description: Backend process P1 may retain location data longer than necessary, increasing exposure risk and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data retention policies are not properly enforced in P1

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Backend process P1 may fail to comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding location data collection, storage, and processing requirements.
assumptions: P1 does not implement required privacy controls or consent mechanisms

title: Linkability of Location Pings Across Time
description: Location pings forwarded from the mobile app backend can be linked across multiple transmissions to reconstruct a user's movement patterns and trajectory over time, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.

title: Identifiability Through Location Data
description: The location pings contain sufficient detail to identify specific individuals or their presence in particular geographic areas, enabling profiling and tracking of users.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The Geofencing Engine may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, potentially exposing sensitive location information to attackers or malicious insiders.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The system may collect more granular location data than necessary for geofencing purposes, violating data minimization principles.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance Risk
description: Processing of location pings may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR or CCPA if proper consent, data retention policies, and user rights are not implemented.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of zone definitions
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in the Family Account Store could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing sensitive location information about family members' daily routines and whereabouts.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain personally identifiable location data that could be used to track family members' movements and infer their schedules.

title: Location-based identifiability of family members
description: Zone definitions could be used to identify specific locations associated with family members, potentially revealing where they live, attend school, or visit friends, enabling tracking of their movements and routines.
assumptions: Zone definitions are unique enough to identify specific locations and can be correlated with family member identities.

title: Unauthorized modification of geofencing zones
description: The Geofencing Engine could have zone definitions modified by unauthorized actors, potentially altering where alerts are triggered or disabling geofencing protections for family members.
assumptions: The geofencing system has insufficient access controls to prevent unauthorized modification of zone definitions.

title: Inaccurate or outdated zone definitions
description: Zone definitions may become outdated (e.g., family moves to a new home, school changes) or contain errors, leading to incorrect geofencing behavior and potentially missing important alerts or triggering false alarms.
assumptions: Zone definitions are not regularly updated and may contain errors from manual entry.

title: Linkability of Movement Patterns
description: The geofencing notification could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movement patterns across multiple zones over time.
assumptions: Notification contains sufficient identifying information to link to specific child

title: Identification of Zone Entry/Exit
description: Unauthorized parties could identify which specific child entered or exited a defined zone based on the notification.
assumptions: Notification contains identifying information about the child

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location-based notifications could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the parent entity.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not adequately secured

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The notification may contain more location and timing data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Notification includes precise timestamps and zone identifiers beyond what's needed

title: Unauthorized Access at Parent Entity
description: The parent entity (EE1) may not have appropriate access controls, allowing unauthorized personnel to view child location notifications.
assumptions: EE1 lacks proper role-based access controls

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's sensitive profile data
description: Child's personally identifiable information (name, DOB, school) and geofence location data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Backend has vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls; data is stored in accessible format

title: Child identification through profile data
description: The combination of child's name, date of birth, and school information could be used to uniquely identify the child, potentially leading to unwanted tracking or profiling.
assumptions: Child's information is publicly accessible or shared across systems; school information is identifiable

title: Linkability of child's data across systems
description: Child's profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., school records, location history) to create comprehensive profiles, potentially revealing patterns about the child's activities and associations.
assumptions: Data is shared or accessible across multiple systems; linking is possible through common identifiers

title: Excessive data collection about child
description: Collecting child's name, DOB, school, and geofence zones may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose of account registration, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: All collected data is stored; geofence zones are retained longer than needed

title: Unauthorized parent account impersonation
description: An unauthorized person could impersonate the parent to create a child's profile, leading to false or malicious data about the child being stored in the system.
assumptions: Parent authentication is weak or compromised; no verification of parent-child relationship

title: Unauthorized Access to Family Account Data
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive family account and child profile information stored in DS2.
assumptions: Inadequate authentication or access controls on the backend system

title: Datastore Breach of Sensitive Family Data
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) could be compromised, exposing account credentials, child profiles, and geofence data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Inadequate encryption or access controls on the datastore

title: Identification of Children from Profile Data
description: Child profile information stored in DS2 could be used to identify specific children, potentially leading to stalking or targeted harassment.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sufficient identifying information

title: Linkability of Child Data to Other Sources
description: Data in DS2 could be linked with other data sources (e.g., location history, school records) to create comprehensive profiles of children and families.
assumptions: Data could be correlated with external datasets

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Storage of child profile and geofence data may violate regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K if proper consent and data minimization are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child data are not fully met

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location data
description: The mobile app backend may disclose the child's current location or location history to unauthorized parties, including third-party services, advertisers, or malicious actors who gain access to the system.

title: Identification through location patterns
description: Location data can reveal sensitive information about the child's daily routines, home address, school, workplace, and frequent locations, potentially enabling identification of the child's identity and personal habits.

title: Unauthorized access to child's location data
description: Unauthorized individuals or systems may gain access to the child's location data without proper authentication or authorization, violating the child's privacy rights.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The system may collect location data beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose of viewing location on a map, potentially storing historical data or tracking movements more extensively than required.

title: Linkability of location data with other personal information
description: Location data can be linked with other personal data (e.g., name, age, contact information) to create detailed profiles of the child, increasing privacy risks through data correlation.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized users or processes without proper authentication and authorization controls, leading to privacy violations.

title: User Identification via Location Patterns
description: Stored location history can be used to identify specific users through patterns such as home/work locations, frequent visits, and movement routines, potentially revealing personal identity.

title: Linkability of Location Data to Individuals
description: Location history data can be linked to specific individuals through timestamps, geographic patterns, and contextual information, enabling tracking of user movements and activities.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Retrieving full location history may exceed what is necessary for serving the map/history view, violating data minimization principles and collecting more personal data than required.

title: Unauthorized User Access via Impersonation
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak, unauthorized users could impersonate legitimate users to access their location history data from the backend process.

title: Linkability of Parent Identity to Child Location
description: When a parent invites a secondary guardian to view child's location, the parent's identity becomes linked to the child's location data, creating a persistent association that could be exploited for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The system logs which parent initiated the invitation and maintains this link in the data flow.

title: Identifiability of Child Through Location Data
description: The secondary guardian can identify the child's identity and routine patterns through location data, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's daily activities, school, and home.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify specific locations and patterns.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Location to Third Parties
description: The secondary guardian may share or leak the child's location data to unauthorized third parties, including other family members, friends, or malicious actors, without the parent's consent.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has access to the location data and may not be bound by privacy agreements.

title: Usurpation of Parent Identity for Location Sharing
description: An attacker could impersonate the parent to invite a secondary guardian, gaining unauthorized access to the child's location data through social engineering or credential theft.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust to prevent identity impersonation.

title: Excessive Location Data Sharing Beyond Necessity
description: The system may share more location data than necessary for the secondary guardian's role, such as historical location data or precise coordinates, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system does not implement data minimization controls for location sharing.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's live location to secondary guardian
description: The backend process shares the child's live location with the secondary guardian without proper verification of authorization or consent, potentially exposing sensitive personal data to unauthorized recipients.

title: Interception of location data in transit
description: The child's live location data transmitted from the backend to the secondary guardian could be intercepted by malicious actors during transmission, leading to unauthorized access to real-time location information.

title: Linkability of location data to child's identity
description: The shared live location data can be linked to the child's identity, enabling tracking of the child's movements and potentially revealing patterns of behavior, school attendance, or home location.

title: Unawareness of data sharing scope
description: Parents or the child may not be fully aware of the extent to which their location data is being shared with the secondary guardian, including duration, frequency, and potential recipients.

title: Secondary guardian misuses location data
description: The secondary guardian may misuse the child's live location data beyond the intended purpose, such as sharing it with third parties, storing it longer than necessary, or using it for unauthorized tracking.

title: Data Leakage Through Improper Handling
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with external advertising partner may contain residual personally identifiable information or be improperly handled, leading to unauthorized data exposure.
assumptions: Partner has adequate security controls; data is truly aggregated; no additional PII is included.

title: Non-compliance Through Consent Issues
description: Users may not have provided explicit consent for their usage data to be shared with third-party advertising partners, violating GDPR or similar privacy regulations.
assumptions: Privacy policy clearly states data sharing; users have been informed; consent mechanisms are in place.

title: Lack of Awareness Through Insufficient Information
description: Users may be unaware that their usage and engagement data is being shared with external advertising/analytics partners, leading to privacy concerns and loss of trust.
assumptions: Privacy policy exists but may not be prominently displayed or easily understood by users.

title: Unintended Consequences Through Misuse
description: Advertising/analytics partner may use the shared analytics data for purposes beyond what was intended by the app developers, such as building user profiles or selling data to other third parties.
assumptions: Partner has contractual obligations; data use is limited to agreed purposes; partner is reputable.

title: Identification Through Data Correlation
description: Even aggregated analytics data could potentially be correlated with other data sources held by the advertising partner or third parties, enabling re-identification of individual users.
assumptions: Data is properly aggregated; partner has no other identifying data; correlation attacks are not feasible.

title: Linkability of Location Data to Child Identity
description: The child's location data combined with check-in/SOS messages can be linked to identify the child's identity and movement patterns over time, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.

title: Identifiability Through Location Data
description: Precise location information in check-in/SOS messages can be used to identify the child's whereabouts, home address, school, and other sensitive locations, enabling tracking of their movements.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The mobile app backend may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, leading to disclosure of the child's location data to third parties, including potential stalkers or malicious actors.

title: Excessive Location Precision
description: The location data may be collected with higher precision than necessary for a check-in/SOS message, violating data minimization principles and exposing more sensitive information than required.
